patients.label: 74-year-old man with comminuted depressed fractures at the base of the middle phalanges of the right middle and ring fingers after a fall

identity_evidence.quote: We present the case of a 74-year-old man

attribution_limitations: The recommendation about implant removal follows the sentence on thin dorsal finger soft tissue and may be a general recommendation rather than a plan for this patient.

The ring finger fracture is called comminuted depressed on radiographs (both digits) and incomplete at the dorsal base of the middle phalanx in the operative text; the two statements may describe different parts of the fracture rather than conflict.

The final follow-up paragraph opens with the 12-month postoperative follow-up for range of motion, but grip strength, the swan-neck deformity, absence of pain, absence of implant discomfort, the DIP joint osteoarthritic change and activities of daily living are stated in later sentences without their own time; the Fig. 6 caption time covers only its range-of-motion statement.

The discussion says the combined approach may be useful in fractures involving multiple digits or osteoporotic bone "as in our case"; the source never states that this patient had osteoporosis or a bone density result.
The radiographic finding of mild osteoarthritic changes in the DIP joint does not name the finger.

limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the eight JPEGs are inspected in the separate visual submission.

Time-governed facts: only text with its own time phrase or a governing figure-caption lead sentence carries a time; grip strength, swan-neck deformity, pain, implant discomfort, DIP joint radiographic change and daily activity status in the 12-month paragraph have no time of their own and stay untimed.
Table 1 (needle gauge specifications) describes equipment in general and is not patient data; it is not recorded as observations.
Author statements about general advantages of the technique, other published methods and rehabilitation protocols (Lalonde, Hintringer) are background, not patient facts.
The source states right-handedness but no structured field holds handedness; it is kept in the case description only.
The 12 range-of-motion values are printed as extension/flexion pairs; the minus sign before DIP extension values is kept as printed and not interpreted.

Traction-type external fixation was judged impractical by the treating team; it is recorded with action unknown (considered, not chosen) and a not_occurred timeline event, not as a patient-declined procedure.
